paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. John asked a straight question: "Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?" (Luke 7:19). Jesus didn't wave it off, He pointed to what was happening: "The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor." (Luke 7:22). Then He added, "Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me." (Luke 7:23).

So what does that teach us? Honest questions can be brought to Jesus, and He answers with what's real. Jesus tells the crowds John is "more than a prophet" (Luke 7:26). The people who had received John's baptism acknowledged God's justice, but the Pharisees and experts in the law "rejected God's purpose for themselves" (Luke 7:29-30), and I think that's a warning for me too.

Then comes the part that stings a little. John came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and people said, "He has a demon!" (Luke 7:33), but the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they said, "Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!" (Luke 7:34). Two totally different messengers, and the SAME answer! So when God's wisdom shows up, friend, don't go hunting for reasons to dismiss it, recognize it and respond, because Jesus closes with, "But wisdom is vindicated by all her children." (Luke 7:35).
